sup-7f96227fe6ee20c6-q2:whole.hint: Separate the reflected part of the incoming sunlight from the part that is absorbed.
notes: Albedo is reflected solar power divided by incident solar power. For an opaque surface, absorbed fraction is 1 − albedo.
Use the same system boundary for numerator and denominator. For a planet, add reflected contributions that leave the planet; do not count outgoing infrared as reflected sunlight.

sup-7f96227fe6ee20c6-q3:whole.hint: Compare the wavelengths of incoming sunlight and radiation emitted by the cooler surface.
notes: Greenhouse gases absorb and emit selected infrared wavelengths associated with molecular energy changes. Much incoming shortwave sunlight passes through the atmosphere.

After an increase in infrared absorption, the planet warms until outgoing energy again matches absorbed sunlight. Avoid describing the greenhouse effect as reflection of all heat or destruction of energy.

sup-7f96227fe6ee20c6-q4:whole.hint: Draw an energy boundary around the whole planet. Which incoming and outgoing arrows cross that boundary?
notes: A spherical planet intercepts sunlight over πR² but emits over 4πR². In the simplest equilibrium model, (1 − α)S/4 = εσT⁴.
At equilibrium, absorbed solar power equals outgoing thermal power. Surface and atmospheric transfers are internal to the whole-planet budget, so do not count them twice.
